Website build.note: Research the two reference sites for real animation/visual patterns, plan a non-slop motion-rich landing build, implement it, then review for quality and AI-slop.

steps.prompt: Open and actually look at reactbits.dev and motionsites.ai (use vision/screenshots, not just text). Extract concrete, reusable patterns: the specific animation primitives and transition ideas reactbits offers (e.g. split-text, blur/scale reveals, magnetic buttons, spotlight/gradient borders, scroll-linked motion, spring easings), and from motionsites.ai the overall visual direction (bold type, dark or high-contrast palettes, generous whitespace, cinematic section reveals, kinetic hero). Deliver a short catalog: (1) 6-10 named motion techniques each with how it feels and a one-line implementation approach, (2) a visual style guide (typography, color, spacing, layout rhythm), (3) a list of what 'AI slop' looks like so we can avoid it (default gradients, centered generic hero, emoji, glassy cards everywhere, stock copy). Be specific and opinionated.
steps.why: vision-capable pass over the reference sites to capture concrete animation/transition techniques and the visual language, so the build copies real craft instead of guessing

steps.prompt: Using the research catalog from the previous agent, write a tight build plan for one promotional landing page that advertises the target website. Define: tech stack (prefer HTML/CSS/vanilla or a lightweight framework with a motion library like GSAP/Framer-style spring easing — pick what installs cleanly and reads as non-AI), section list (hero, value prop, features/showcase, social-proof/CTA, footer), the exact motion treatment per section mapped to the researched techniques, the type/color/layout system from the style guide, and an explicit 'anti-slop' checklist to enforce. Output file structure and the order of implementation. No code yet.
steps.why: turn the research catalog into a single coherent, buildable site architecture before touching code

steps.prompt: Implement the site exactly per the previous agent's plan and the research techniques. Requirements: high-craft scroll and entrance transitions, spring-based easing (no linear/janky default tweens), a distinctive hero with kinetic type or reveal, cohesive dark/high-contrast visual language, real intentional copy (no filler), reduced-motion accessibility, responsive layout, and clean hand-written CSS. Avoid every item on the anti-slop checklist. Keep dependencies minimal and the project runnable. Deliver the full working files.
steps.why: implement the animated landing site from the approved plan

steps.prompt: Adversarially review the previous agent's output as a demanding design + code reviewer. Check: do the transitions actually feel premium and intentional (easing, timing, stagger) or are they default/cheap? Is any AI-slop present (generic hero, stock copy, lazy gradients, emoji, cookie-cutter cards)? Are motion, accessibility (prefers-reduced-motion), responsiveness, and the visual system consistent? Does it clearly advertise the target website? List concrete, prioritized fixes and rewrite any weak copy or motion. Confirm the project builds/runs.
steps.why: catch AI-slop, weak transitions, and correctness gaps in the built site before shipping
